title: Cotangent transitivity and vanishing for a ring retraction
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings and $j:R\to S$, $r:S\to R$ ring homomorphisms with $r\circ j=\mathrm{id}_R$. Use the standard cotangent complexes and their square-induced maps [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] in the ordinary-module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; derived extension of scalars is the universal total left derived functor of termwise tensor extension [def-weil-module-base-change]. Then $L_{R/R}$ for the identity map is a zero object, and the canonical transitivity triangle for $R\xrightarrow j S\xrightarrow r R$ has the form $L_{S/R}\otimes_{S,r}^{\mathbf L}R\longrightarrow L_{R/R}\longrightarrow L_{R/S}\longrightarrow (L_{S/R}\otimes_{S,r}^{\mathbf L}R)[1]$, with zero middle object. In particular, if $L_{R/S}=0$ for the map $r$, then $L_{S/R}\otimes_{S,r}^{\mathbf L}R=0$ in $D(R)$. No flatness, finite generation or Tor-vanishing hypothesis on $j$ or $r$ is imposed.

proof.text: For the identity $R\to R$, take the constant simplicial $R$-algebra $Q_\bullet=R$, the polynomial algebra on the empty set. By [lem-trf-constant-polynomial-resolution-retraction] it is a polynomial resolution with identity augmentation. The comparison of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] identifies $L_{R/R}$ with $s(\Omega^1_{Q_\bullet/R}\otimes_{Q_\bullet}R)$. Every $R$-derivation out of $R$ is zero, since it vanishes on each element of the image of the identity. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] therefore gives $\Omega^1_{R/R}=0$: its identity endomorphism corresponds to the zero derivation and hence equals the zero endomorphism. All terms of the displayed differential complex are zero. Its image in $D(R)$ is a zero object, so $L_{R/R}=0$.

source.place: Tag 08QH (lemma-cotangent-complex-polynomial-algebra), empty-variable case; Tag 08QI (remark-resolution), constant polynomial resolution; Tag 08R1 (lemma-bootstrap), vanishing of L_{B/B}.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle] to the triple $R\xrightarrow j S\xrightarrow r R$. Put $X=L_{S/R}\otimes_{S,r}^{\mathbf L}R$, $Y=L_{R/R}$ and $Z=L_{R/S}$. Since $r\circ j=\mathrm{id}_R$, the middle term is the cotangent complex of the identity map, so step 1 makes $Y$ a zero object. The cited theorem gives the canonical distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow uY\xrightarrow vZ\xrightarrow dX[1]$ in $D(R)$, with the standard square-induced first two arrows. Its theorem applies to arbitrary ring maps, so no flatness or Tor hypothesis has entered.

Assume now $Z=L_{R/S}=0$. Apply clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to the distinguished triangle of step 2 with $W=X[1]$ and $c=\mathrm{id}_{X[1]}$. Its hypothesis is $u[1]\circ c=0$, which holds because $Y=0$ and the additive shift sends a zero object to a zero object. We obtain $k:X[1]\to Z$ with $\mathrm{id}_{X[1]}=d\circ k=0$, since $Z=0$. Applying the inverse additive shift $[-1]$ of [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives $\mathrm{id}_X=0$. Thus every map into or out of $X$ is zero (compose with its identity), and the zero maps between $X$ and the zero object are inverse isomorphisms. Consequently $X=0$ in $D(R)$, as asserted.
